validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, extensively documented project. Docketed as Ohio Power Siting Board Case No. 16-0253-GA-BTX ('C314V Central Corridor Pipeline Extension Project'), litigated to the Ohio Supreme Court (In re Application of Duke Energy Ohio, Inc., Slip Opinion No. 2021-Ohio-3301, decided 2021-09-22, affirming the certificate) and referenced again in a 2026 Ohio Supreme Court rate-recovery opinion (2026-Ohio-2064) which states Duke 'completed construction of the pipeline and officially placed it into service on March 14, 2022.' Also confirmed by Duke Energy's own construction-progress newsletter (Jan 2022), and independent local press (Cincinnati Enquirer, WCPO, Fox19, WVXU) and municipal government pages (Village of Golf Manor). Correctly classified as an operating natural-gas distribution/transmission pipeline (built to transmission-line safety standards per the Ohio Supreme Court opinion) owned/operated by Duke Energy Ohio, a Duke Energy subsidiary -- not a duplicate of any other roster row (no other US-gas row in this 46-row roster describes a Hamilton County, Ohio, Duke Energy project). Owner1 = 'Duke Energy' (the parent, 100%) is a reasonable identification, though the actual certificate holder/applicant of record in every source is 'Duke Energy Ohio, Inc.' (the operating utility subsidiary) -- proposing 'Duke Energy Ohio' as the Operator (separate blank field) rather than re-litigating Owner1. Opened/read to exhaustion: all 9 wiki-harvested citations for P0297 (1 dead landing page, 1 generic EIA aggregate page that never names this pipeline [name_found=false, useless as support], 1 Duke progress-report PDF, 5 local-press articles, 1 Duke PR release) plus 9 additional independently-found sources (2 Ohio Supreme Court opinions, 1 Court News Ohio summary, 1 Golf Manor municipal page, 2 WCPO articles, 1 Fox19 2021 article, 1 SEC 10-Q XBRL filing, 1 PSU Shale Law Weekly Review). Total 18 documents opened.

validity.recommendation: correct LengthKnown from 12 to 13 (best-supported as-built figure); note genuine 12-14 mi spread across otherwise-credible sources
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC: GEM's current Length=12 mi is contradicted by its OWN cited source. The wiki cites ref [4] (Duke's Jan-2022 progress-report newsletter) for Length=12mi, but that PDF actually says 'The entire 13-mile pipeline is currently undergoing...' and 'Approximately 13 miles of pipeline installed' -- i.e. the cited document says 13, not 12. Independently: WCPO (2019, board-approval article) -- 'The 13-mile-long pipeline'; WCPO (2021, construction-start article) -- 'the pipeline will span 13 miles from Golf Manor to Sycamore Township's northern annex'; WVXU (2019) -- 'the nearly 13-mile, 20-inch diameter pipeline'; Duke's 2018 PR Newswire application release -- 'approximately 13 miles long and 20 inches in diameter'. Against that: Cincinnati Enquirer (2021, construction-start) and Fox19 (2021, construction-start) both say '12-mile', and a separate WCPO headline (on the 2021 Ohio Supreme Court ruling) says '12-mile pipeline' though its own body text clarifies this is the ROUTE-LENGTH FLOOR from Duke's original 2016 notice-of-intent ('at least 12 miles'). The Ohio Supreme Court's slip opinion (2021-Ohio-3301) states the certified routes 'run approximately 13 to 14 miles,' and Court News Ohio's summary of that same opinion calls it a '14-mile' pipeline. Reading all of this together: 12 miles is the earliest (2016 notice-of-intent) rough estimate, 13-14 is the certified-route range, and Duke's own AS-BUILT completion report (the source GEM itself cites) says 13. The weight of evidence -- including the very document GEM cites -- supports 13, not 12. Tier=medium (multiple sources agree on 13, but a genuine 12-14 mi spread exists across otherwise-credible reporting, so this is not a clean single-value confirmation).

validity.recommendation: Capacity=1.03 MMcf/d is unsupported by any source found, including GEM's own cited reference for it -- blank the value (or re-verify against the OPSB record) rather than keep an unsourced figure
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC: gem.wiki cites the same ref [4] (Duke's Jan-2022 progress-report newsletter, cite_note-:1-4) for Capacity: 1.032 Mmcf/d as it does for Length. I fetched and read that PDF in full (pdftotext -layout): it is a two-page construction-progress newsletter that discusses hydrotesting, restoration schedules and contact information -- it contains NO capacity, flow, or Mcf/MMcf figure of any kind. I also checked the older Duke landing-page ref [2] (now 404; its 2017 Wayback snapshot contains no mile/inch/capacity terms either -- likely JS-rendered content the crawler didn't capture). I then searched independently (PR Newswire x2, WCPO x2, Fox19 x2, WVXU, Cincinnati Enquirer, Golf Manor municipal page, both Ohio Supreme Court opinions, Court News Ohio, PSU Shale Law Weekly Review, SEC 10-Q XBRL filing) -- none states a capacity/throughput figure in MMcf/d or Mcf/d for this pipeline. A design pressure of ~400 psig IS well documented (see Pressure fill below), but pressure and capacity are not interchangeable and no source converts one to the other for this line. 1.03 MMcf/d would also be implausibly small for a 20-inch, 13-mile transmission-grade line built specifically to 'balance natural gas supply' for a system serving ~450,000-529,000 customers and replace propane-peaking plants that supplied ~10% of peak-day demand -- the physical scale argues against this number on its face, independent of the sourcing problem. Given the cited source does not contain this value and no independent source states it, I could not corroborate 1.032 MMcf/d at all; recommend treating it as unsourced pending a check of the OPSB certificate record itself (which was not fully retrievable in this pass) rather than keeping it silently.

Found a real cost source but did not stage a value because it is a RANGE, not a point figure, and I did not want to invent a midpoint: Duke Energy Ohio's SEC 10-Q XBRL filing for the period ended 2021-06-30 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/17797/000132616021000216/R52.htm) discloses, under 'Duke Energy Ohio | Natural Gas Pipeline extension | OPSB,' an 'Estimated capital cost excluding AFUDC' of $163 million (minimum) to $245 million (maximum), alongside 'Number of conditions on construction: 41' -- which cross-confirms this is the Central Corridor project, since the Ohio Supreme Court opinion states the OPSB certificate carried exactly 41 conditions. (An older, pre-redesign estimate of ~$110 million also circulates in secondary sources but predates the final 20-inch/400psig design and the 2019 certificate, so I did not use it.) Recommend Baird decide how to record the range (e.g. midpoint ~$204M, or the minimum $163M as the more conservative documented figure, SegmentCostUnits=USD, SegmentCostYear=2021) rather than my picking a number the source itself doesn't state. url_verifier's content screen doesn't find 'Central Corridor' on this XBRL page (it never uses that name, only 'Natural Gas Pipeline extension'/'OPSB'), so I did not add it to proposed_refs pending that decision -- URL: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/17797/000132616021000216/R52.htm.
